title: How Coding Agents change Software Development Forever - Hailong Zhang
talk_summary: The talk describes async coding agents, especially a PR-triggered unit-test agent called Guru, and argues for narrow problem definitions, eval harnesses, per-stage model choice, task-specific context, and a shared agent OS. It reports modest production acceptance (~50% of Guru PRs merged) and heavy internal use (~80% of tests), with humans reviewing agent PRs.

takeaways.technique: Narrow problem plus eval harness first
takeaways.what_they_do: They insist on a concrete, doable problem and build a dataset and evaluation harness before working on models, context, and orchestration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: unit test is a problem, but software engineering is not a problem

takeaways.what_they_do: They evaluate models on different scenarios and may use different LLMs for different stages within the same job.
takeaways.evidence_quote: even within the same job, Guru may use different LLMs for different stages

takeaways.what_they_do: They build context per language/framework and gather issues, reviews, commits, PRs, readme, and code, then filter/select it to fit the context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all this information need to be gathered together and to be filtered and to be selected to fit into the context

takeaways.what_they_do: Guru is triggered by a PR, detects changed code, decides whether tests need adding/changing, writes and runs tests, and submits a PR with summary and coverage improvement for human review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Guru will detect the change of the code and determine if this change needs more unit test
takeaways.numbers: over 50% of PRs merged/accepted; handles around 80% of unit tests in its own repo

takeaways.what_they_do: They abstract common runtime, tools, and context so domain agents can be built quickly instead of from scratch.
